candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the HTTP parameters consumed by UserManager.parseProfile() (loginname, password, fullname, email) on the self-registration/self-profile-edit flow. Supplying a full name such as "Adm inistrator" (space or other whitespace inserted) passes the STANDARD input check, does not collide with the exact-string login-name/full-name uniqueness checks, and yields the wiki name "Administrator".
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked the duplicate-name defenses: setUserProfile() does check findByLoginName() (line 298) and findByFullName() (line 309), and validateProfile() re-checks login/full name and e-mail; none of them inspects the derived wiki name. Checked InputValidator.STANDARD (UNSAFE_PATTERN, line 52): it rejects quotes, brackets, ':', '&', '@', ';', '{', '}', '%', '$', backslash and control characters, but it does not reject whitespace, so "Adm inistrator" passes validation. Checked validateProfile()'s find(fullName) branch (lines 535-543): it does not match "Adm inistrator" and only errors when the value equals another profile's login name but not its full name, so it does not block this. Verified that WikiPrincipal.equals() (lines 126-133) and Group.findMember() (lines 325-336) compare names only (the type is irrelevant), that GroupManager.isUserInRole() accepts any non-Role/GroupPrincipal as a user principal, and that asserted (unsigned cookie) sessions are not 'authenticated' and therefore cannot use this path directly - the attacker must register/authenticate, which is the default flow. Also confirmed the Admin group is created with the member string "Administrator" (Installer.ADMIN_NAME, lines 57-58 and 150-162) and that the shipped install text states the default policy gives Admin group members AllPermission (CoreResources.properties lines 185-187).
candidates.impact: A remote, unprivileged user (or any existing low-privilege account that edits its profile) can obtain AllPermission on the wiki - i.e. full administrative control (delete/restore pages and attachments, manage users, groups and security-relevant settings), which is a direct privilege escalation and confidentiality/integrity/availability compromise of the wiki instance.
candidates.prerequisites: Default custom authentication (UserDatabaseLoginModule) with the normal self-service profile save/reload path (jspwiki.approver.workflow.createUserProfile not configured, which is the default so no approval is required), a wiki that has been installed so the Admin group exists with member "Administrator", and the default jspwiki.policy that grants AllPermission to group Admin (documented in the shipped install messages). No special privilege is needed before the attack.
candidates.root_cause: DefaultUserProfile.setFullname() computes the user's wiki name by deleting all whitespace from the user-supplied full name (WHITESPACE = "\\s"). UserManager.setUserProfile() checks uniqueness of the login name, full name and e-mail, but never of the derived wiki name, and findByWikiName() is only used for lookups, never for a duplicate check. At login, AbstractUserDatabase.getPrincipals() injects the wiki name as a WikiPrincipal(WIKI_NAME), and group membership is decided purely by name: GroupManager.isUserInRole() -> Group.isMember() -> Group.findMember() compares only Principal.getName() (WikiPrincipal.equals() is also name-only). WikiSession.injectGroupPrincipals() therefore adds GroupPrincipal("Admin") to a session whose WIKI_NAME principal is "Administrator", and AuthorizationManager.allowedByLocalPolicy() grants that group principal the AllPermission defined for group Admin in the default jspwiki.policy.
candidates.title: Privilege escalation to AllPermission via wiki-name collision with the Admin group member
candidates.trace: 1) POST profile fields: fullname="Adm inistrator" (or any whitespace-separated spelling of the target name), unique loginname/password/email. 2) UserManager.parseProfile() stores fullname verbatim; DefaultUserProfile.setFullname() sets fullName="Adm inistrator" and wikiName="Administrator". 3) UserManager.setUserProfile() rejects duplicates only via findByLoginName() and findByFullName(); "Adm inistrator" matches neither the real "admin" login nor the real "Administrator" full name, so the profile is saved. 4) On login/auto-login, WikiSession.injectUserProfilePrincipals() calls UserDatabase.getPrincipals(), which adds WikiPrincipal("Administrator", WIKI_NAME). 5) WikiSession.injectGroupPrincipals() -> GroupManager.isUserInRole() -> Group.isMember() matches the wiki-name principal against the Admin member "Administrator" and adds GroupPrincipal("Admin") to the subject. 6) AuthorizationManager.checkPermission()/allowedByLocalPolicy() evaluates the local policy with that GroupPrincipal; the default policy's AllPermission grant for group Admin now applies, giving the attacker full administrative rights.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-verified. The snapshot contains no JSP/test sources and no jspwiki.policy file, so the exact registration JSP call sequence (validateProfile then setUserProfile) and the concrete AllPermission grant in the deployment's policy file are inferred from the Java APIs, Installer and shipped resource strings rather than directly observed. The Admin group member name is "Administrator" for an installer-created wiki; a differently named admin/group member would require the attacker to match that name instead.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization / CWE-269 Improper Privilege Management (name-only authorization over an attacker-derived identifier with no uniqueness check)

coverage_summary: get_source_scope reports 1001 model-visible files from the assigned root, with no sensitive-path/symlink exclusions and a binary/NUL guard; the same filters apply to B0 and P1. I read or searched the main Java modules (jspwiki-main, jspwiki-util, jspwiki-markdown), the WAR/JSPWiki descriptors (web.xml), jspwiki.properties, classmappings.xml, CoreResources and the bundled user/group XML files. Coverage focused on authentication/authorization (login modules, UserManager, UserDatabase, WikiSession, GroupManager, AuthorizationManager, Installer), servlets/filters (AttachmentServlet, WikiServlet, WikiJSPFilter, WikiServletFilter, WikiAjaxDispatcherServlet, RPCServlet, AtomAPIServlet), page/attachment providers, XML/JDBC storage, the markup parser/link parser, and utility classes. The snapshot contains no JSP or test sources, so the web UI layer and the default jspwiki.policy file could not be inspected directly. Not every one of the 1001 files was read line-by-line (e.g. most of the 87 KB JSPWikiMarkupParser, RSS/Atom, workflow, and several plugins were only spot-checked).
limitations: No JSP sources and no jspwiki.policy file are present in the snapshot, so the registration/profile-edit call sequence and the exact default AllPermission grant for group Admin are inferred from Java APIs, Installer and resource strings, not directly observed.
No runtime execution, tests or container deployment was possible; all findings are static source traces and none is runtime-confirmed.

The wiki-name-collision finding assumes the standard deployment where the Admin group contains the principal name "Administrator" (installer-created) and where profile self-registration/self-editing is permitted (default configuration); the snapshot does not include the policy file that would prove the final grant.

Only one candidate could be submitted; the XML-database injection and deserialization leads are real code weaknesses but their end-to-end attacker control could not be established from the snapshot alone.
The repository appears partially stripped (no JSP/test trees); coverage of the intended deployable web application is therefore incomplete.

rejected_leads.lead: XML injection in XMLUserDatabase.saveDOM(): user profile attributes (fullName, email, etc.) are written into userdatabase.xml with no XML escaping (lines 358-405), and the file is re-parsed by DocumentBuilderFactory with entity expansion enabled (lines 303-349); an injected <attributes> node would feed Serializer.deserializeFromBase64() -> ObjectInputStream.readObject() (XMLUserDatabase lines 677-692, Serializer lines 60-71).
rejected_leads.reason: Attacker control is doubtful on the normal profile-save path: the XML metacharacters needed for the injection ('"', '<', '>', '&', ';', '\'', etc.) are all rejected by InputValidator.STANDARD (UNSAFE_PATTERN line 52) that UserManager.validateProfile() applies to login name/full name, and no in-repo caller passes raw profile fields to XMLUserDatabase.save() without that validation. Kept as an unconfirmed lead, not the selected candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: XML injection in XMLGroupDatabase.saveDOM(): the group 'modifier' attribute is written with no escapeXml() although name/creator/member are escaped (lines 422-444), and the modifier is the current user principal name.
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable only by a user who may create/edit groups, and the injected value is the same profile name string; the impact chain is longer than the selected candidate and no concrete exploit primitive was traced. Unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE in XMLUserDatabase / XMLGroupDatabase: DocumentBuilderFactory is configured without disallow-doctype-decl or external-entity restrictions (XMLUserDatabase lines 303-313, XMLGroupDatabase lines 257-266).
rejected_leads.reason: By default the XML files are administrator-controlled deployment artifacts; no remote attacker path to write a DOCTYPE into them was established.

rejected_leads.lead: Path traversal in CookieAuthenticationLoginModule.getCookieFile(): the JSPWikiUID cookie value is used directly as a file name under workDir/logincookies (lines 175-215), so a cookie like '../../<file>' reads an arbitrary readable file and uses its content as the authenticated login name.
rejected_leads.reason: jspwiki.cookieAuthentication is off by default; the read content is used as a login-name principal, and the impact (info-leak or account takeover) depends on files whose content matches a target login name. Lower confidence and lower impact than the selected candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Open redirect via AttachmentServlet.validateNextPage(): the check only rejects values containing '://' that do not start with the base URL (lines 434-449), so a scheme-relative value such as '//evil.example' or a base-URL prefix like 'http://wiki.evil.example' passes and is passed to sendRedirect (lines 304, 418, 426).
rejected_leads.reason: Genuine logic gap but only an open-redirect/phishing impact, and container handling of protocol-relative Location values varies; weaker than the privilege-escalation candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: ShortURLConstructor.getForwardPage() uses the request parameter 'do' unvalidated as the JSP to forward to (lines 221-227), and WikiServlet forwards to '/'+jspPage (WikiServlet lines 88-101).
rejected_leads.reason: Only active with the non-default short-URL constructor and the attainable impact (which resources can be forwarded to) is container-dependent; not traced to a concrete privilege bypass.

summary: Reviewed the JSPWiki 2.11.0-M3-git snapshot defensively from source only (Java modules jspwiki-main, jspwiki-util, jspwiki-markdown, war descriptors/properties; 1001 files, no test/JSP sources present). Strongest source-supported issue: the wiki name is derived from the user-supplied full name by deleting whitespace, is never checked for collisions, and is later used as an authorization-relevant principal name, so a self-registering user can pick a full name such as "Adm inistrator" whose derived wiki name equals the default Admin group member "Administrator" and thereby obtain the group's default AllPermission. One candidate is submitted; several other plausible-but-weaker leads (XML injection/deserialization in the XML user database, XXE in the XML databases, cookie-auth path traversal, open redirect, short-URL forward) are listed as rejected/unconfirmed.
